name: Mount Rainier Skyline Trail
unique: A 14,410-foot glaciated volcano with wildflower meadows at 6,000 feet, and a loop trail that puts Rainier, the Tatoosh Range and a waterfall in one frame.
buzz: The wildflowers in late July are legendary; the trail is crowded and the altitude is real. Start early for parking.

name: Hoh Rainforest
unique: A temperate rainforest of moss-draped maples and Sitka spruce, with the Hall of Mosses and a river the color of green glass.
buzz: People whisper in the Hall of Mosses; it is genuinely otherworldly. Rain is likely and part of the experience.

name: Pike Place Market
unique: A century-old public market on a bluff above the sound: fish throwing, the original Starbucks, a gum wall and a maze of levels that rewards wandering.
buzz: Go at 8am before the crowds and eat at a counter; the fish throw is a photo op, the produce is the real thing.

name: San Juan Islands Orca Kayak
customer: Wildlife people, couples, families with teens
unique: Paddle the Salish Sea among the San Juan islands, with resident orcas, humpbacks, porpoises and bald eagles — and no guarantee of any of them.
buzz: Guides are excellent on whale-watch rules; the kayak is quieter and closer than a boat. Sightings are luck, so book two days.

name: Leavenworth
unique: A failing logging town remade itself as a Bavarian village, with nutcrackers, bratwurst, accordion music and the Cascades as a backdrop.
buzz: It is kitsch executed with real commitment; Oktoberfest is a mob and the Christmas lights are genuinely charming.

name: North Cascades
unique: Jagged peaks, turquoise glacial lakes and more glaciers than any other park in the lower 48, with a highway that crosses three dams and a pass.
buzz: People call it the American Alps and note how empty it is; the trails are steep and the weather changes fast.

name: Palouse
unique: Rolling loess hills planted in wheat, lentils and canola, forming green and gold waves that look like a painting from the ridge roads.
buzz: Photographers plan around harvest and sunrise; the back roads are gravel and the towns are tiny. Steptoe Butte is the viewpoint.

name: Deception Pass
unique: A bridge 180 feet above a churning tidal channel between two islands, with cliffs, old-growth forest and sea lions below.
buzz: The bridge walk is free and thrilling; the currents are dangerous for swimming. Sunset from the bridge is the shot.

name: Mount St. Helens
unique: The volcano that blew its top in 1980, with a crater, a lava dome, a buried forest and a visitor center that shows the blast minute by minute.
buzz: The Johnston Ridge view is extraordinary on a clear day; clouds can erase everything. Check the webcam before driving.

name: Crater Lake
unique: The deepest lake in the country, filled by rain and snow alone, so blue it looks artificially saturated, with a cinder cone island in the middle.
buzz: The Rim Drive is spectacular and the water is freezing; Cleetwood Cove is the only swim and the climb out is steep.

name: Multnomah Falls
unique: A 620-foot two-tier waterfall right off the highway, with a footbridge across the middle and a trail to the top through mossy basalt.
buzz: It is the most photographed waterfall in Oregon and the parking is a nightmare; go before 8am or take the shuttle.

name: Hood River Windsurfing
unique: The Columbia River Gorge funnels steady 25-knot wind between basalt cliffs, making it the windsurfing and kiteboarding capital of North America.
buzz: Schools are good with beginners and the scene is friendly; the current and the wind are humbling. Book a two-day lesson.

name: Timberline Lodge
unique: A WPA-era lodge hand-built by craftsmen on Mount Hood, with the only year-round ski area in North America and a fireplace you can stand in.
buzz: The lodge is a masterpiece and the summer skiing is a novelty; terrain is moderate. The Ram's Head bar is the apres spot.

name: Cannon Beach and Haystack Rock
unique: A 235-foot sea stack rising out of the surf, tide pools full of anemones and starfish, and a wide flat beach backed by forest.
buzz: The tide pools at low tide are the attraction; it is windy and often foggy, which is the mood. Go at sunset.

name: Portland Saturday Market
unique: The largest continuously operating open-air crafts market in the country, under a bridge on the Willamette, with food stalls and buskers.
buzz: The crafts are genuinely handmade; the food row is the lunch move. It is crowded by noon.

name: Willamette Valley Wine Country
unique: Rolling hazelnut hills planted with Pinot Noir, with tasting rooms that range from barns to architectural statements and a terroir that beat Burgundy in 1979.
buzz: Pinot is the specialty and the smaller wineries are the charm; book the famous ones and drive carefully.

name: Smith Rock
unique: The birthplace of American sport climbing: welded tuff spires and arêtes above the Crooked River, with 1,800 routes and a Misery Ridge trail that scrambles to a view of the Cascades.
buzz: Climbers call it a cathedral; the hiking is steep and the grades are stiff. Guides are good for first-timers.

name: Ashland Shakespeare Festival
unique: A repertory company doing Shakespeare, new plays and musicals in an Elizabethan outdoor theater and two indoor stages, in a town that takes it seriously.
buzz: Production quality is consistently excellent; the outdoor theater in summer is magical. Book a package with a talkback.

name: Oregon Dunes Sandboarding
unique: The largest coastal sand dunes in North America: 500-foot slopes you can sandboard, slide or ride in a dune buggy down to the ocean.
buzz: Sandboarding is harder than snowboarding and the rental shops give good tips; go early when the sand is firm.

name: Powell's City of Books
unique: A city block of new and used books, color-coded rooms, a rare book room and a map at the door because you will get lost.
buzz: Book people treat it as a pilgrimage; the used section is the joy. The cafe is a good place to sit with a find.

name: Pendleton Round-Up
unique: A century-old rodeo with a grass arena, a teepee village on the edge of town and a parade that shuts the whole city down.
buzz: The grass arena makes the riding wilder; the Happy Canyon night show is a piece of living history. Book early.

name: Half Dome
unique: A 14-to-16-mile climb up granite stairs and cables to a summit that drops 4,800 feet to the valley floor on three sides.
buzz: The cables are the crux and the permit lottery is the gatekeeper; altitude and heat stop more people than fear. Train for it.

name: Alcatraz Night Tour
company: National Park Service / Alcatraz City Cruises
unique: The cellhouse after dark, with ranger talks in the solitary wing and a boat ride back past the city lights — the tour that makes the prison feel like a place people lived.
buzz: The night tour is worth the extra over the day trip; book weeks ahead. The audio tour by former inmates is excellent.

name: Monterey Bay Aquarium
unique: A kelp forest three stories tall, a million-gallon open-ocean tank with tuna and sharks, and a sea otter exhibit that is impossible to leave.
buzz: The kelp forest and jellies are the icons; it is expensive and timed entry is essential. Go at opening on a weekday.

name: Joshua Tree Night Sky
unique: Dr. Seuss trees, granite boulders and a sky so dark the Milky Way is a texture, two hours from Los Angeles.
buzz: The night sky is the reason to stay over; the boulders are a climber's playground. Summer heat is dangerous.

name: Salvation Mountain
unique: A painted adobe mountain covered in Bible verses and flowers, built by one man over thirty years in the desert near Slab City.
buzz: It is sincere, free and deeply strange; respect the artist's rules and bring water. Combine with Bombay Beach.

name: Winchester Mystery House
unique: A Victorian mansion with stairs that go nowhere, doors that open onto walls and 160 rooms, built by the heiress to the Winchester rifle fortune to confuse the spirits.
buzz: The story is better than the house; the tour is scripted and the house is genuinely odd. Go for the lore, not the frights.

name: Santa Cruz Beach Boardwalk
unique: A 1907 seaside boardwalk with the Giant Dipper wooden coaster and a 1911 carousel, both national landmarks, right on the sand.
buzz: The Giant Dipper still delivers; the boardwalk is free to walk and the food is fairground-grade. Skip summer weekends.

name: Coachella
unique: A desert polo field turned into a fashion show and a festival, with giant art installations, a Ferris wheel and headliners under the stars.
buzz: The production is unmatched and the heat, walking and prices are brutal; the campgrounds are their own scene.

name: Magic Castle
unique: A Victorian mansion where magicians perform close-up in parlors and on stages, with a dress code, secret doors and a strict no-photos rule.
buzz: People call it the best night out in LA; admission requires an invite from a member or a hotel booking. Dress up.

name: Glass Beach
unique: Three coves where decades of dumped glass were polished by the surf into pebbles of green, amber and blue.
buzz: Take photos, leave the glass — it is illegal to remove and the beach is shrinking. Go at low tide.

name: Burney Falls
unique: A 129-foot waterfall fed by underground springs that pour from the cliff face itself, so it flows at full volume even in drought.
buzz: Teddy Roosevelt called it the eighth wonder; the loop trail is short and the mist is refreshing. Combine with Lassen.

name: Avenue of the Giants
unique: A 31-mile road threading through old-growth redwoods, with trees wide enough to drive through and a canopy that turns daylight green.
buzz: People drive it twice; the Founder's Grove and the drive-through tree are the stops. It is cold and damp even in summer.

name: Disneyland
unique: The original park, still the best-executed theme park on earth: Pirates, the Haunted Mansion, Indiana Jones and a level of detail that rewards looking up.
buzz: Disney adults plan months out and still get surprised; the app, the lightning lane and the food are all part of the game. Go midweek.

name: Big Sur Highway 1
unique: Ninety miles of cliff-edge highway above the Pacific, with redwood canyons, a purple sand beach and the Bixby Bridge.
buzz: The drive is the attraction; pull-offs are the whole point. Check for landslide closures before you go.

name: Trestles Surf
unique: A cobblestone river mouth that produces one of the most rippable waves in California, reached by a dirt path through a state park.
buzz: Locals are protective but the wave is forgiving; dawn patrol is the etiquette. Lessons are worth it for first-timers.

name: Getty Center
unique: A travertine hilltop campus by Richard Meier with Van Gogh's Irises, a cactus garden and a tram ride above the 405.
buzz: Free admission and the architecture compete with the art; the garden is the peaceful corner. Parking is the cost.

name: Mammoth Mountain
unique: A 11,053-foot volcano with the longest season in California, steeps above treeline and a town of hot springs and breweries below.
buzz: Locals ski in shorts in May; the top is wind-scoured and the lower mountain is friendly. Book lodging early.

name: Death Valley
unique: The hottest, driest, lowest place in North America: salt flats, sand dunes, a crater and a lake that appears once a decade.
buzz: Winter is the only sane season; distances are huge and cell service is nil. Badwater at sunrise and the dunes at dusk.

name: Mendenhall Glacier Ice Caves
unique: Paddle across a glacial lake and walk into caves of blue ice under a retreating glacier, with the cave roof shifting every season.
buzz: Guides are strict about safety and the caves change yearly; the paddle is calm and the ice is surreal. Book early.

name: Denali Flightseeing
unique: A bush plane lands on a glacier at 7,000 feet on the flank of North America's tallest mountain, with crevasses and icefall below.
buzz: The glacier landing is the upgrade everyone remembers; weather cancels often, so book early in your trip.

name: Iditarod Start
unique: Seventy dog teams leave downtown Anchorage in a blizzard of barking for a 1,000-mile race to Nome, with handlers, fans and snow machines everywhere.
buzz: The ceremonial start is free and joyful; the real race start in Willow is quieter. Dress for -20.

name: Chena Hot Springs
unique: Outdoor rock pools at 106 degrees in the boreal forest, with an ice museum, a geothermal power plant and aurora overhead on winter nights.
buzz: The aurora viewing from the hot springs is the draw; the resort is rustic and the drive is long. Bring a hat.

name: Knik Glacier Airboat
unique: An airboat runs up a glacial river through icebergs to the face of a hanging glacier, with moraine, meltwater and no road in.
buzz: The ice and scale are startling; the ride is loud and cold. Ask about the ice cave add-on.

name: Alaska Railroad Glacier Discovery
unique: A domed train through moose country, across a glacier-fed river and into a canyon where the track clings to the cliff, with a whistle-stop flag service.
buzz: The dome car is worth it; the ride is long and the scenery nonstop. Book the Coastal Classic for the best single day.

name: Utqiagvik Polar Plunge
unique: Jump into the Arctic Ocean at the northernmost town in the United States, where the sun does not set and the water is barely above freezing.
buzz: It is a bucket-list bragging right and a genuinely strange place; travel is expensive and logistics are real.

name: Brooks Falls Brown Bears
unique: Brown bears stand in the lip of a waterfall and catch sockeye salmon mid-air, from a viewing platform a few dozen yards away.
buzz: The single best bear-watching experience on earth; access is by floatplane and permits are limited. Book a year ahead.

name: Kenai Fjords
unique: A boat through tidewater glaciers that calve into the sea, with sea otters, puffins, humpbacks and orcas in the same afternoon.
buzz: The glacier calving is the moment people remember; seasickness is common outside the bay. Take the longer tour.

name: Road to Hana
unique: Six hundred curves and fifty-nine one-lane bridges through rainforest, waterfalls and black-sand beaches, with banana bread stands and no hurry.
buzz: Start before 6am, drive one way and swim at the stops; the back road is rough and rental agreements may forbid it.

name: Haleakala Sunrise
unique: Watch the sun rise above the clouds from a 10,023-foot volcanic summit, then bike or hike down through a crater that looks like the moon.
buzz: The 3am alarm and the cold are real; reservations are required and sell out. The crater hike is better than the sunrise for some.

name: Molokini Snorkel
unique: A partially submerged volcanic crater with 150-foot visibility, a coral reef inside the curve and turtles on the outside.
buzz: Morning trips beat the wind and the crowds; the crater is protected and the fish are tame. Seasickness is possible.

name: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park
unique: An active volcano you can drive around, with steam vents, a lava tube and, when the eruption is on, glowing lava entering the sea.
buzz: Check the eruption status before you go; the crater rim drive is excellent regardless. Bring rain gear.

name: Manta Ray Night Snorkel
unique: Giant manta rays with 12-foot wingspans loop within inches of your mask at night, feeding on plankton in the beam of a surfboard light.
buzz: People call it the best wildlife encounter in Hawaii; the water is calm and the mantas are habituated. Book a small boat.

name: Waimea Canyon
unique: The Grand Canyon of the Pacific: a ten-mile gorge of red and green, with lookouts, goats on the cliffs and a trail into the kalalau valley.
buzz: The colors are unreal after rain; the drive up is steep and the clouds roll in by noon. Go early.

name: Na Pali Coast Kayak
unique: Seventeen miles of fluted green cliffs dropping into the Pacific, with sea caves, dolphins and a beach landing at Kalalau.
buzz: It is a serious paddle with open-ocean crossings; guides are excellent and the scenery is unmatched. Not for beginners.

name: Pearl Harbor
unique: The USS Arizona Memorial floats above the sunken battleship, with oil still seeping from the hull, plus the Missouri and a submarine you can board.
buzz: The Arizona is free but timed and somber; the aviation museum and the Missouri are the add-ons. Book the free tickets early.

name: North Shore Surf
unique: The Seven Mile Miracle: Pipeline, Sunset and Waimea in a row, where the world's best surfers ride waves that can close out the bay.
buzz: Watch from the beach in winter and surf the gentler breaks in summer; respect the locals and the reef.

name: Kalaupapa Mule Ride
unique: Ride a mule down 1,700 feet of sea cliffs on a switchback trail into the isolated peninsula where Hansen's disease patients were exiled for a century.
buzz: The history is devastating and the ride is genuinely thrilling; the settlement tour is led by residents. Book far ahead.

name: Mauna Kea Stargazing
unique: A 13,796-foot summit above a third of the atmosphere, with observatories, sunset above the clouds and a sky that reveals the Milky Way's dust lanes.
buzz: Altitude sickness is real and tours handle the acclimatization; the summit at sunset is cold and unforgettable. Book a tour with parkas.

name: Hanauma Bay
unique: A flooded volcanic crater with a coral reef and tame reef fish, a short bus ride from Waikiki, with a marine education center and strict capacity limits.
buzz: Reservations open two days ahead and vanish; go at opening for clear water. The reef is recovering and the rules matter.
